asked: the operator, 2026-11-25 07:33 and 07:47: two worker groups for the study's best law inside its own study, one pushing N as high as possible (and on the top contenders too) and the other perturbing it at random to explore its neighbourhood, the smallest moves too, so that a law sensitive to its exact parameters is told from one that depends on its seeds; once the neighbourhood is confirmed and the top N does not invalidate the result, find the boundaries of the law's zone; and the folder doing both by itself, without switching between studies; the outliers only once every scoring law is mapped or inside a mapped region (08:04 and 08:07)

neighbourhood.why: moves of every parameter at once by a radius times a draw between a half and one, at random signs. A law's random streams are drawn from its own fingerprint, so any move, however small, also runs it on new streams: the rings of 1e-9 to 1e-3 cannot change the physics of a law that is not on a knife edge, and are read beside its seeds (below). In study 175 (bundle of 2026-11-24 08:35Z) a perturbation kept its holder's outcome in 92% of cases at 1e-9, 96% at 0.001, 89% at 0.01 and 71% at 0.1, and one holder, aba936bffa (175's H12), read another outcome in 4 of 4 at 1e-9 and at 0.001: two thirds alike at 0.1 is a region above that noise, and 16,384 the first size every kind is read at, so the neighbours run to it and no further

seeds.why: the law itself again on twice the design's seeds (0 to 5), to the neighbourhood's read: seeds 0 to 2 are its own campaign's again, the same streams, so they show the run reproduces; seeds 3 to 5 are new. Each seed is read alone at 16,384, with the law's own campaign's three. Its seeds disagree: it depends on its seeds. They agree but a move of 1e-3 or less reads another kind: it is sensitive to its exact parameters. Both agree: robust (the operator, 2026-11-25 07:47: "being able to tell the difference is I feel important")

outward.why: where every neighbour reads the law's kind, a ring at twice the largest radius, until one differs or 0.8; a relative move under 1 never flips a coupling's sign, so the terms a law holds stay the same (the term axis is a later build)

boundaries.why: each neighbour of another kind at 0.01 or beyond is joined to the law by a line halved four times where the kind flips, as study 176's map does: the boundary known to a sixteenth of the line

depth.why: the focus law and the study's best five by score, each run again from 64 to one size past the study's 65,536 (the operator, 2026-11-14 19:58: one size at a time, 262,144 first). A seed's save is JSON of its chains' edges, 19 s at 65,536 and mean degree 32, so about 76 s at 262,144, inside the 120 s a stop waits for it, and about 5 min at 1,048,576, outside it: 1,048,576 waits on the save. Since 873 (the operator, 2026-11-25 13:11: "always just 1 worker thread responsible for always pushing the memory limit to the system max (+ its free buffer zone ofc) but automatically testing how far N is feasible/safe to run without getting oom killed") the ladder is open to 4,194,304: each next size is priced from the law's own peak memory at the two sizes below (growth between linear and quadratic, 10% kept over) and bought only when it fits the host's reach with its free 10 GiB kept, else the law is settled at its memory ceiling (operations/depth_reach.py, decisions/memory_ceiling.py); a seed's save holds its chains' edges packed, so 1,048,576's save fits the stop's grace

next.why: when a law's focus ends (mapped, unconfirmed or invalidated), the next best law by score that has not had one begins in the same three campaigns, unless it lies inside a region already mapped: of the same kind, and nearer a mapped law than half the largest radius at which every one of that law's neighbours read its kind (a distance measured as `research/neighbourhood.distance`, the relative step of every parameter, root mean square). Score decides where the compute goes first (the operator, 2026-11-25 08:07); when every scoring law is mapped or inside a mapped region, the outliers come next (862)
